summary: Two levers, both inside the compute-allocation family, moved the metric. First, the 5-minute budget is step-starved at the baseline's 524K-token batch: halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (grad_accum 1) took val_bpb 1.012347 -> 1.000800 with no other change, while going further to 2**17 regressed to 1.010210, so ~262K tokens/step is the optimum. Second, with the batch fixed, scaling the model from depth 8/dim 512 to depth 10/dim 640 gave the largest single gain, 1.000800 -> 0.988145 at only 34.6GB VRAM. Scaling past that failed in every direction tested: depth 12/dim 768 = 0.994653, depth 10/dim 768 = 0.991023, depth 12/dim 640 = 0.990440, so 10x640 is a real local optimum and the earlier 8->10 gain came from depth, not the width bundled with it. Next I would retune the optimizer to the new operating point rather than the shape: Muon matrix_lr and the embedding LRs were never re-swept after the batch halved and the model grew, and the warmdown fraction (0.5) and value-embedding budget (5 full-vocab embeddings at depth 10) are both untested at this configuration.
